lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- What I Can and Can't Do Yet
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna de Fátima | Lesson 6 -- What I Can and Can't Do Yet
lesson.grammar_point: can and can't for ability and permission, plus could for a polite request

listenings.text: Good morning, everyone. Ray Collins, with the rules for this week. Please listen, because the badges change on Monday. If you have a green badge, you are a visitor. You can walk on the yellow walkway with a guide, and that is all. You cannot go into the tunnel and you cannot operate anything. Blue badge: you have access to every area at ground level, and to the tunnel, if you have the training for confined spaces. Red badge: you can operate the machines, because you have the license for them. One more thing. Nobody signs a paper for another person. If you need permission for a new area, come and ask me, and I sign it myself. Thank you, and have a safe week.

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. Good news from London: I finished the training last Friday, so I have the blue badge now. A year ago I was only a visitor here, and I waited at the gate with a green card in my hand. This week I can go down into the tunnel with my own crew, and I can sign the daily report. I still cannot operate the big machines. For that you need a license, and the course is six months long. Oh, and one favor: could you send me a photo of your badge? Ours are changing next month, and my supervisor wants to see how other sites do it. Thank you, and talk to you soon.

extra_audio.text: Giovanna arrives at the gate at seven o'clock. She shows her badge to the guard. The guard checks her training and opens the gate. She signs the book for the visitor from London. Then she asks: could you give him a green badge, please?

paras: Everybody stops at the same gate in the morning, and everybody shows a badge. The badges are not the same color, and the color is not decoration: it says what each person is allowed to do and which areas they can go into. Green, blue, red.

Marcos has a green badge. He is a visitor from the city office, and he comes twice a month. He can walk on the yellow walkway, but only with a guide. He cannot go into the tunnel, and he cannot operate anything, not even the small lift. At the entrance he signs his name in a book, and he gives the badge back before he goes home.

Amanda has a blue badge. She is an engineer, like you, and she has access to every area at ground level and to the tunnel, because she has the training for confined spaces. She can sign the daily report. She cannot operate the big machines: that is a different license, and she does not have it.

Tomas has a red badge. He has the license for the excavator, so he can operate it all day, in the tunnel and on the surface. But his access to the office area is only with permission, and he asks for it politely every time: "Could I use the meeting room for ten minutes?" Each new skill on his card is one more thing he can do on this site.
Nobody at this gate can do everything. That is the point of the three colors: together, the three of them can.
